name: mcp-supertoinette
description: MCP server for Supertoinette. Read French recipes and rescale their quantities. No API key required.
long_description: Supertoinette has published French recipes since 2002. This server reads one by the number in its address and returns the ingredients, the method, the times, the difficulty and the cost the site publishes. What it takes care over is what the page does not say: the site writes a time it does not display as zero, so a time comes back null rather than as no time at all; it repeats the last step of every recipe in its structured block, so the steps are read from the list the page prints; and it links each ingredient line to a page of its own choosing, which sometimes names a different ingredient, so that link travels as the site's own rather than as the identity of the ingredient. Quantities can be rescaled to any number of servings, and every line then says whether the arithmetic landed exactly, had to move to stay an amount a kitchen can measure out, or carried nothing that could be multiplied. Read-only, no API key and no account.

tools.name: search_recipes
tools.description: Search by a dish or an ingredient, with the categories the site counts beside the results and the identifier to read each recipe.

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.description: Read one recipe by the number in its address: ingredients, method, times, difficulty and cost, rescaled to a number of servings on request.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List the categories the site browses its recipes by, each with the token that opens its listing and where the site printed it.

tools.name: browse_recipes
tools.description: Read one category's recipes page by page, with the difficulty and the total time the site prints beside each.

tools.name: get_wine_pairings
tools.description: Read the five wines the site ranks for a dish, in its own words, or one page of its alphabetical index of dishes.

tools.name: scale_ingredients
tools.description: Rescale a French ingredient list offline, saying of each line whether the result is exact, rounded to stay usable, or nothing that could be multiplied.
